text:
sara: FYI customer AcmeHealth hitting lots of 504s on hosted inference since ~10:12 UTC. They report API p95 ~18-22s and occasional 5xx gateway errors.

jess: Thanks. Any tenant id / example request?

sara: tenant=acme-prod. Customer shared a sample request (long seq ~8k tokens with streaming). They say it started after a traffic uptick.

priya: I pulled the gateway traces for acme-prod. Queue depth peaked at 120 (limit 128) and continuous-batching backlog grew to 42k tokens queued. Dequeue p95 jumped to 14s.

marc: That sounds like continuous-batcher backlog + KV cache miss churn. Are their requests creating many long prefixes?

li: Customer confirmed they started a bulk job that streams many multi-turn long sequences; Observed many requests with sequence_length > 6k.

jess: Can someone paste the gateway logs snippet for the 504s?

priya: Log snippet:
```
[10:13:02] gateway: request_id=abc123 tenant=acme-prod dequeue_ms=14230 queue_depth=120 cpu_ms=500 error=504 backend=continuous-batcher
[10:13:03] gateway: request_id=abc124 tenant=acme-prod dequeue_ms=19670 queue_depth=121 error=504 reason=tail_timeout
```

marc: Looks like tail-latency timeouts from batcher. Continuous-batcher didn't coalesce fast enough; KV cache hot-swapping causing extra latency.

sara: Customer wants a fast remediation. They are on hosted plan. Any quick mitigations?

priya: Short term: enable per-tenant queue shedding and route acme-prod to an alternate model variant with lower memory/latency (quantized). That will reduce per-token kernel time. I can push a route override.

jess: Also can we temporarily bump acme-prod queue depth soft-limit to 160 and enable aggressive early-reject on extra-long sequences?

marc: Bumping queue depth risks other tenants; prefer routing them to a dedicated less-loaded pool or applying request-level throttling. If customer agrees, we can move them to a spare dedicated pool for 30m.

li: Customer approved slower throughput if it avoids 5xx. They prefer throttling + model variant.

priya: Plan: 1) Apply tenant-level throttling (rate limit long-seq requests) 2) Route acme-prod to model:rw-v2-quantized-1 as fallback 3) Short-term route override and monitor. I'll apply step 1 & 2 now.

deploy-bot: rollout started by priya: route-override(acme-prod -> rw-v2-quantized-1) @ 10:32 UTC

ops-bot: metric alert suppressed for acme-prod 30m by jess to avoid noise during mitigation

priya: Done. Initial verification: dequeue p95 dropped to 4.2s, queue_depth steady ~40, no new 504s in the last 6m.

sara: customer said errors dropped immediately. They still see higher latency than usual but acceptable.

marc: Follow-ups: - run batcher profiling to identify KV eviction hotspots - add heuristic early-reject for sequences > 7k tokens - consider autoscale burst for hosted on this tenant pattern

jess: I'll create a customer-facing summary and cc billing if cost spike expected.

billing-bot: note: routing to rw-v2-quantized-1 is billable; estimated incremental cost +12% for acme-prod this window.

sara: I relayed to AcmeHealth and they accepted the tradeoff. Closing incident if no regressions in 1h. Thanks team :thumbsup:

priya: adding runbook note and a short repro for eng: steps to reproduce (internal):
1) spawn 50 parallel streaming requests with sequence_length ~6-9k for tenant=acme-prod
2) observe queue_depth and dequeue_ms on /debug/queue?tenant=acme-prod
3) inspect batcher logs for kv-eviction spikes

marc: I'll pick up the profiler work.

jess: Great. Marking as mitigated, will reopen if errors recur.

sara: incident thread closed for now.
